title: Progressive Semantic Anchors - personal pad
content:
Topline idea:
Progressive Semantic Anchors (PSA) = lightweight session summarization + anchored tokens stored in KV cache keyed by semantic centroid rather than full prefix. Goal: keep high-utility context while bounding KV size growth for long-running sessions.

Why this?
- Problem: sessions with many turns blow up KV cache and increase per-token cost / memory pressure; naive truncation loses important context and hurts quality.
- Hypothesis: a small set of "semantic anchors" (dense vectors + short textual pointers) per session can preserve intent / facts needed for generation while keeping sequence lengths small.
- Expected benefits: lower latencies (smaller KV transfers), cost reduction (less compute per step), fewer quality regressions vs fixed token truncation.

Quick sketch of UX / flow:
1) On session creation: PES = empty anchor set.
2) On each user message / assistant response: compute embedding(s) for the new chunk and decide whether to create/update an anchor.
3) Anchors contain: short label (8-30 token pointer), embedding centroid, last-updated timestamp, importance score, optional compact summary (1-2 sentences).
4) At inference time: instead of passing N previous turns, runtime passes current turn + top-K anchors (by relevance) as a condensed context.
5) Anchors are stored in customer-scoped cache (hosted/dedicated/private) with TTL and size quotas.

Design choices to think through (open):
- Anchor granularity: per-turn vs micro-chunk vs server-side summary blocks. Heuristic: create anchor when new-turn embedding distance > threshold or when message contains entity/assertion patterns.
- Anchor summaries: auto-generate via short-shot summarization or extractive token selection? Tradeoff: generation costs vs fidelity.
- Relevance ranking: cosine similarity on embeddings is fastest; consider adding recency boost and importance weight.
- Eviction policy: combined semantic distance & LRU vs fixed-size prioritized by importance score.
- Consistency across rollouts: how to handle anchor schema changes without invalidating sessions.
- Privacy: anchors are derived from user messages; need to represent as customer data with KMS tagging and retention controls.

API/Config surface (rough):
- SessionConfig.progressiveAnchors: {enabled: bool, maxAnchors: int, embedModel: string, scoreThreshold: float, summaryMode: ["none","extractive","abstractive"], evictionStrategy: string}
- Runtime flags: passAnchorsAs: ["inline","attachment-token","system-prompt"], allowAnchorMutate: bool
- Console: per-session anchor viewer, per-model anchor hit/miss metrics.

User stories (draft):
- As a developer, I want long chat sessions to maintain key facts so my assistant doesn't lose the conversation thread, while keeping latency reasonable.
- As a platform engineer, I want anchors to live within per-tenant quotas and to have observable hit rates and memory amplification metrics.
- As a compliance officer, I want control over retention for anchors and to be able to redact anchors on customer request.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics (for a pilot):
- Functional: PSA can be toggled per-project and returns top-K anchors with relevance scores in the API response.
- Quality: for a set of benchmark dialogs, answers with PSA enabled have <= 5% degradation in task accuracy vs full-history and > 20% improvement vs naive truncation.
- Latency/cost: median inference latency decreases by >= 10% for long sessions (> 30 turns); tokens sent in prompt reduced by >= 40% on average.
- Ops: anchor storage per-session stays under maxAnchors * anchorSize and evictions logged; anchor hit rate reported.

Experiment plan (MVP):
Phase 0: Offline sim
- Run PSA prototype in offline evaluation harness. Use existing convo logs, simulate anchor creation rules, and compare generation quality with full-history baseline and fixed token-window baseline.
- Metrics: accuracy/regression on evals, average prompt token count, anchor storage distribution.

Phase 1: Internal dogfood (hosted projects)
- Enable PSA for internal teams only, with conservative defaults (maxAnchors=6, summaryMode=extractive).
- Collect metrics and qualitative feedback.

Phase 2: Beta with select customers (Dedicated + Hosted)
- Add console controls and retention policy features. A/B test against full-history for 2-3 apps with long chat sessions.

Implementation notes / infra considerations:
- Embeddings: pick a small, fast embed model for anchor vectors to avoid large overhead (e.g., small open model). Consider batching embed calls.
- Anchor schema: store as small proto/json with embedding as base64 or float32 array truncated; store pointer to summarization result if abstractive.
- Runtime integration: serving-runtime must be able to accept an anchors argument and incorporate them into the tokenization/attention plan without increasing KV hot-path latency. Might be implemented as an early-merge step that rewrites prompt.
- Backfill: consider tools to backfill anchors for existing sessions (inspection vs re-generating summaries).
- Observability: add per-session metrics: anchorsCreated, anchorsEvicted, anchorHitRate, avgAnchorDistance.
- Resource limits: per-tenant anchor budget, throttle anchor summarization during bursts.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Will semantic anchors bias future model outputs (overfit to anchors)? Need to test hallucination risk.
- How does anchor usage interact with function-calling / tool-invocation flows where tool context is canonical?
- Security/PGP: embedding values leak state; need privacy review with security team for hosted product.
- UX: do developers prefer to see anchors as explicit objects in the session API or prefer opaque optimized prompts?

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype offline script to ingest 10k conversation segments and simulate anchors. (owner: Harper)
- [ ] Slack eng-serving-runtime to sync on API shape and perf constraints. (owner: Harper)
- [ ] Talk to Maya about summarization cost tradeoffs and to Noah on metrics pipeline. (owner: Harper)
- [ ] Draft small Confluence page with evaluation results and example request/response for console.

Rough notes/ideas for later:
- "Anchor templates" that map to persona facts vs task facts so we can treat different anchor types differently (task-critical anchors nondiscardable).
- Anchor diffing: store change-set of anchors to make rollbacks trivial during canary rollouts.
- Tiny client-side summarization: move summarization into SDKs for private deployments to reduce server cost and privacy exposure.

Random scratch thoughts (raw):
- Could combine with prefetching: when anchor relevance spike predicted, prefetch extra token slices to GPU memory.
- Use anchors as part of quality evals: sample responses when anchor hit==false to detect missing anchors.

End of pad. Will iterate after offline sims.
